title: Color palettes with AI

body.text: Claude helps build a palette from the
brand's personality: tell it the mood, the target audience, and the industry
— you get primary, secondary, and accent colors with hex codes, the color-psychology reasoning, and pairs to avoid.

example: "Build a palette for a finance-education brand aimed at first jobbers: trustworthy but not stuffy, approachable, with hex codes and reasoning"

title: Check the colors' accessibility

body.text: Pretty colors alone aren't enough — have Claude
check the contrast ratio against WCAG (normal text needs 4.5:1 or higher)
and simulate how a color-blind person sees your palette. Colors that can't be told apart need another cue, like an icon or pattern.

example: "Check every color pair in this palette for WCAG AA; for any that fail, suggest a close shade that passes"

question: What info helps the AI build an on-brand palette?

options.text: The brand's mood, target audience, and industry

question: What's the minimum contrast ratio for normal text under WCAG AA?
If two colors in a chart can't be told apart by a color-blind person, what should you do?

options.text: Add another cue, like an icon or pattern

question: When building a color palette with AI, what must you always check?

options.text: The largest possible number of colors
The accessibility of the color pairs, e.g. enough contrast
Everyone, including people with impaired vision, must be able to read it
